newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on exports, cold weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on exports, cold weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a relatively strong export number for corn in USDA's weekly export sales report and on cold weather in the U.S., traders said.
"Corn export numbers were decent," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of corn for the week ended December 12 totaled 700,900 tonnes, roughly 200,000 tonnes above the previous week. But the sales number was within the range of trade expectations of 700,000 to 900,000 tonnes which limited the bullish impact.
"The export numbers were great for everything, especially beans," a trader said.
Cold weather in the U.S. which was boosting feed usage by the U.S. livestock also was supportive, sources said.
The posting of 2.1 million bushels of wheat Thursday for delivery on the December contract was factored into Wednesday's market, some traders noted.
The CBOT December contract expired quietly at 1201 CST and settled at $2.69-1/2, down 1-3/4 cents.
Corn closed two cents per bushel higher to 1/4 lower, with March up 1-1/4 at $2.66.
Rosenthal Collins sold 3.5 million bushels of March and Cargill Inc bought one million March, traders said. SAK Futures and Tenco Inc also bought one million bushels of March, they said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 47,000 contracts, well below the 83,711 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, SAK Futures sold 200 March $2.50 puts at 2-1/4 cents, Produce Grain sold 200 March $2.70 puts at 10-1/2 cents and bought 200 March $2.70 calls at five cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 14,000 contracts, below the 22,271 contracts traded Wednesday.
